codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.rootCause: Ensure-KILMStudioEndpointReachable's own retry budget (30*2s=60s) was shorter than the managed LM Studio starter's genuine first-run contract (up to ~120s), and the starter's own process/exit code was never observed -- reproduced live during the 2.5.0 Greenfield acceptance run.
codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.fix: The starter is now the authoritative start/timeout contract: the default retry budget is sized to its own up-to-120s window, and its process/exit code is tracked so a real starter failure surfaces immediately instead of being outlived by continued polling.
codexLocalLmStudioTimingFix.validation: Test-KIStackCodexLocal.ps1: a static assertion on the shipped default values plus fast behavioral checks (starter exit code observed, genuine timeout still fails). Negative control confirmed.

ragLiveTargetValidation.scope: Execute (Add/Query/Replace/Remove) and Rollback of Add, Replace, and Remove all verified against a live OpenWebUI 0.11.0 instance with before/after remote evidence, each including a repeated Rollback call confirmed as a clean idempotent no-op.
ragLiveTargetValidation.regressionFinding: A partial-failure-then-retry regression test for the Replace/Remove restore path (added 2.6.0 AP01, mirroring the pre-existing Add-path scenario) found a real defect: a retry could re-issue a remove call against remote content an earlier partial attempt had already deleted, failing the retry itself. Fixed in Remove-RAGRemoteEntry to treat an already-removed target as already-satisfied, matching the real server's own behavior; negative-control verified.

findings.description: A .partial file already at the exact expected size was previously re-requested with an end-of-file Range header, causing HTTP 416 from the source. Fixed to verify such a file directly via the existing size/SHA256 contract with no HTTP request; a hash mismatch fails safely through the existing invalid-artifact contract.

targetSystemMutationNote: RAG Execute created one isolated test Knowledge collection on the live target; Rollback (verified idempotent on a repeated call) genuinely deleted the remote file and Knowledge collection, and the local test fixture was removed -- net state fully reverted, confirmed via pre/post remote file-existence and knowledge-collection checks. This is separate from the physical Greenfield installer run recorded under results.greenfieldAcceptance, which targeted a disposable Hyper-V VM, not the persistent real target machine referenced here. Separately, the 2.7.0 Codex Local LM Studio timing fix's live-target validation stopped and let the managed starter restart the real target's local LM Studio API server (GUI left running throughout) -- net state fully reverted (server reachable again, same as before); the starter-failure-path proof used a synthetic starter under a disposable scratch directory only, never the real production starter. For 2.8.0, the managed OpenWebUI update acceptance ran two real administrator-elevated Complete Installer Upgrade transactions against C:\KI-Stack with kernel-config.json temporarily retargeted to 0.10.2 and back to 0.11.0 (reverted exactly in the source repo afterward, byte-identical to the committed state), and genuinely downgraded then upgraded the real OpenWebUI venv package via Update-KIStack-OpenWebUI.ps1 -- net state fully reverted to the pinned 0.11.0, confirmed via direct venv version readback and a passing HTTP healthcheck. The pre-existing five accumulated stale/misplaced CutoverRuntime payload zips under installer/complete were also genuinely reduced to one by the payload-hygiene fix during these same real runs, which is the intended, permanent end state, not something reverted. For 2.9.0, the ReplayComponent acceptance ran a real, interactive, administrator-elevated Start-KIStackCompleteInstaller.ps1 -ReplayComponent openwebui-visual-pack transaction against the already-compliant real Visual Pack on C:\KI-Stack: this genuinely re-ran the existing Visual Pack install/validate path (real backup created, real API key entered interactively as a SecureString and never persisted, real browser-based first-login/API-key flow, real image and video generation tests both passing) and left the target functionally unchanged (same pinned Visual Pack version, same OpenWebUI/ComfyUI health, no second venv or other unexpected mutation) -- this is the intended, idempotent end state of a Replay, not something requiring reversion. For 2.10.0, the Update-KIStack-All acceptance was a single read-only -CheckOnly run against C:\KI-Stack: it queried the real installed/pinned state of every managed component plus a real PyPI upstream lookup for OpenWebUI, and performed no mutation whatsoever -- the real target's genuine drift (OpenWebUI already at 0.11.1 against the 0.11.0 pin) was observed and reported, not corrected, by design.
